content:
The New Student

When Adaeze joined our class in the middle of the term, she was very shy. She sat alone during break and spoke to nobody. Some of the pupils laughed at her because she spoke with a different accent. One day, our teacher, Mr Eze, asked Adaeze to read a poem in front of the class. Her voice was clear and beautiful, and everyone listened quietly. After she finished, the whole class clapped. From that day, Adaeze made many friends. She joined the debating society and later won a prize for the best speaker in the school. Adaeze taught us that we should not judge people by their appearance or accent.

opts: She was afraid of the teacher

She did not like the school

content:
The Market Day

Every Saturday is market day in our town. Traders come from far and near with their goods: yams, plantains, vegetables, cloth, and pots. The market is always busy and noisy. Buyers haggle over prices, and sellers call out to attract customers. My mother goes to the market early in the morning to buy fresh vegetables. She says that the early buyer gets the best goods at the lowest prices. In the afternoon, the market becomes quieter as traders pack their unsold goods and return to their villages. Market day is important to our town because it brings people together and helps farmers to sell their produce.
